name: Mary
overview: Mary of Rome, a female figure mentioned by the Apostle Paul in Romans 16:6, is recognized within Scripture though little else is recorded about her background or tribe. Her mention highlights her presence in the early Christian community in Rome. Beyond this, no additional personal details or notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Mary is a proper name that carries various meanings including 'bitterness,' 'plump one,' 'wished-for child,' and 'one who loves or is loved.' This range of meanings reflects the richness of the name in Hebrew tradition, though it was not given directly by God in this instance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Mary of Rome beyond her identification in Romans 16:6. No other familial or relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mary of Rome's significance lies in her mention by the Apostle Paul, indicating her role and presence within the early church community in Rome. This attests to the active participation of women in the life of the first-century Christian assembly. Her inclusion by Paul underscores the importance of faithful believers who supported the ministry and fellowship of the church.
